world: the earth and all its people and things
The trouble starts when the body's clock and the world's clock disagree.
needs: The garden needs watering twice a week during summer.
systems: sets of things working together as connected wholes
Several legal systems now recognise rivers as having rights.
noticing: the act of becoming aware of or observing something
Noticing small changes early can prevent bigger problems later.
pausing: stopping briefly before continuing an action
She read the whole report aloud without pausing once.
briefly: She paused briefly before continuing her speech to the crowd.
walls: upright structures that enclose or divide a space
Two parallel hard walls will bounce a sound back and forth, producing a buzzing rattle.
know: to have information or understanding about something
Do you know the fastest way to get to the airport?
what: used to ask for information about something
The reason lies in what cities are actually made of.
caution: great care taken to avoid danger or mistakes
Drivers should proceed with caution on the icy road.
